claim: ATUM enables imaging of serial sections deposited on thick plastic tapes by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
source: Like other volume electron microscopy approaches, automated tape-collecting ultramicrotomy (ATUM) enables imaging of serial sections deposited on thick plastic tapes by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characteristic of ATUM.

claim: ATUM is unique in enabling hierarchical imaging and thus efficient screening for target structures, as needed for correlative light and electron microscopy.
source: ATUM is unique in enabling hierarchical imaging and thus efficient screening for target structures, as needed for correlative light and electron microscopy.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature of ATUM in the abstract.

claim: SEM of sections on tape can only access the section surface, thereby limiting the axial resolution to the typical size of cellular vesicles with an order of magnitude lower than the acquired xy resolution.
source: However, SEM of sections on tape can only access the section surface, thereby limiting the axial resolution to the typical size of cellular vesicles with an order of magnitude lower than the acquired xy resolution.
evidence: This limitation of SEM imaging on tape is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: Serial-section electron tomography (ET) yields isotropic voxels at full EM resolution.
source: In contrast, serial-section electron tomography (ET), a transmission electron microscopy-based approach, yields isotropic voxels at full EM resolution
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of ET in the abstract.

claim: Serial-section electron tomography requires deposition of sections on electron-stable thin and fragile films, thus making screening of large section libraries difficult and prone to section loss.
source: but requires deposition of sections on electron-stable thin and fragile films, thus making screening of large section libraries difficult and prone to section loss.
evidence: This limitation of ET is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: In ATUM-Tomo, sections are first reversibly attached to plastic tape via a dissolvable coating, and after screening detached and transferred to the ET-compatible thin films.
source: To combine the strength of both approaches, we developed 'ATUM-Tomo, a hybrid method, where sections are first reversibly attached to plastic tape via a dissolvable coating, and after screening detached and transferred to the ET-compatible thin films.
evidence: This describes the key methodological innovation of ATUM-Tomo as stated in the abstract.

claim: Microthrombi and associated sites of BBB leakiness were identified by confocal imaging of injected fluorescent and electron-dense nanoparticles.
source: Microthrombi and associated sites of BBB leakiness were identified by confocal imaging of injected fluorescent and electron-dense nanoparticles, then relocalized by ATUM-SEM, and finally interrogated by correlative ATUM-Tomo.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: Volume electron microscopy provides high-resolution data of target structures that can be used to render complex biological morphologies in three dimensions.
source: Volume electron microscopy (EM) provides high-resolution data of target structures that can be used to render complex biological morphologies in three dimensions (Peddie et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Array tomography techniques, such as ATUM, have proven particularly powerful for correlating specific biological structures.
source: Among the available volume EM approaches, array tomography techniques (Wacker and Schroeder, 2013), such as ATUM (Kasthuri et al., 2015), have proven particularly powerful for correlating specific biological structures (Schifferer et al., 2021; Snaidero et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations in the introduction.

claim: In ATUM-SEM, a reel-to-reel system transfers the sections from the diamond knife onto tape.
source: In ATUM-SEM, a reel-to-reel system transfers the sections from the diamond knife onto tape (Kubota et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the ATUM-SEM process with citation support.

claim: High-resolution imaging by array tomography is currently restricted by physical sectioning, resulting in typical voxels of 3 × 3 × 30–100 nm.
source: High-resolution imaging by array tomography is, however, currently restricted by physical sectioning, resulting in typical voxels of 3 × 3 × 30–100 nm, where SEM determines the lateral resolution of ≈3 nm.
evidence: This limitation of array tomography is explicitly stated in the introduction.

claim: Array tomography can reveal fine cellular processes down to ≈40 nm, but potentially misses smaller subcellular structures, such as vesicles or contact sites that can be hidden within a section volume.
source: As a consequence, array tomography can reveal fine cellular processes down to ≈40 nm, but potentially misses smaller subcellular structures, such as vesicles or contact sites that can be hidden within a section volume.
evidence: This describes the resolution limitations of array tomography.

claim: In electron tomography, semi-thick sections (200–400 nm) are tilted in the electron beam and Fourier transformed for image reconstruction.
source: In ET, semi-thick sections (200–400 nm) are tilted in the electron beam and Fourier transformed for image reconstruction (Baumeister et al., 1999; Young and Villa, 2023; Frank, 2006)
evidence: This describes the ET process with citation support.

claim: ATUM could not be combined with ET because the former necessitates attaching sections on a solid support, while the latter as a projection method, needs sections to be deposited on electron-transparent films.
source: So far, ATUM could not be combined with ET because the former necessitates attaching sections on a solid support, while the latter as a projection method, needs sections to be deposited on electron-transparent films.
evidence: This explains the technical incompatibility between ATUM and ET prior to this work.

claim: At the BBB, the actual barrier function is determined by distinctive ultrastructural features, mostly within the endothelial layer, including tight junctions, pinocytosis, and vesicular transport.
source: At the BBB, the actual barrier function is determined by distinctive ultrastructural features, mostly within the endothelial layer, including tight junctions, pinocytosis, and vesicular transport (O'Brown et al., 2019; Andreone et al., 2017; Nahirney et al., 2016; Hirano et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes BBB ultrastructure with citation support.

claim: Controlled cortical impact in mice is a model for traumatic brain injury that involves BBB damage.
source: Controlled cortical impact in mice is a model for traumatic brain injury that involves BBB damage.
evidence: This describes the experimental model used in the study.

claim: LNDs and colloidal gold particles of similar size (30 nm) and surface chemistry (PEGylation) ensure similar biodistribution.
source: To mark sites of vessel injury, we injected LNDs and colloidal gold particles of similar size (30 nm) and surface chemistry (PEGylation) ensuring similar biodistribution.
evidence: This describes the experimental design rationale.

claim: LNDs and gold particles accumulate in microthrombi formed in the impact penumbra within 30–60 min post-injection.
source: LNDs are highly fluorescent, while gold is electron dense – and both accumulate in microthrombi formed in the impact penumbra within 30–60 min post-injection (Khalin et al., 2022)
evidence: This describes the behavior of the injected nanoparticles with citation support.

claim: Tissue preservation was ensured by imaging for a maximum of 1 hr, followed by gentle removal of the cover slip by floating-off in the buffer.
source: Tissue preservation was ensured by imaging for a maximum of 1 hr, followed by gentle removal of the cover slip by floating-off in the buffer.
evidence: This describes a methodological precaution taken in the study.

claim: A typical 1000-section library was collected, which could then be imaged hierarchically and repetitively.
source: A typical 1000-section library was collected, which could then be imaged hierarchically and repetitively.
evidence: This describes the scale of the section libraries generated.

claim: The microclot consisted of luminal erythrocyte stalls in combination with platelets and immune cells.
source: The microclot illustrated here consisted of luminal erythrocyte stalls (Figure 1D and G) in combination with platelets and immune cells (Figure 1D and H).
evidence: This describes the cellular composition of microthrombi observed in the study, with reference to figures.

claim: An accumulation of platelets, interspersed with filamentous, electron-dense fibrin was found in the center and at the ends, 'plugging' the occlusion.
source: An accumulation of platelets, interspersed with filamentous, electron-dense fibrin was found in the center and at the ends, 'plugging' the occlusion (Figure 1D, F and H).
evidence: This describes the ultrastructural features of microthrombi with reference to figures.

claim: Gold particles and brighter but less discrete particles of the same size, presumably representing LNDs, were detected between luminal cells.
source: Correlating to the fluorescence pattern, we detected gold particles and brighter but less discrete particles of the same size, presumably representing LNDs, between luminal cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the localization of nanoparticles observed in the study.

claim: At sites of extravasation indicated by an LND halo, a neutrophil undergoing diapedesis was found.
source: In contrast, at sites of extravasation indicated by an LND halo, we found a neutrophil undergoing diapedesis (Figure 1E) and abluminal gold particles in its proximity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This describes a specific observation at sites of BBB leakage.

claim: Abluminal gold particles were found in proximity to the neutrophil undergoing diapedesis.
source: In contrast, at sites of extravasation indicated by an LND halo, we found a neutrophil undergoing diapedesis (Figure 1E) and abluminal gold particles in its proximity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This describes the spatial relationship between immune cells and nanoparticles.

claim: Within the microthrombus periphery, regions of the endothelium were swollen with intact tight junctions, while in the core, regions with almost no discrete endothelial layer prevailed.
source: Within the microthrombus periphery, regions of the endothelium were swollen with intact tight junctions, while in the core, regions with almost no discrete endothelial layer prevailed (Figure 1H).
evidence: This describes the heterogeneous endothelial morphology at microthrombi.

claim: Colloidal gold was found at pathologically thinned endothelium, basement membrane, and in pericytes.
source: Colloidal gold was found at pathologically thinned endothelium, basement membrane, and in pericytes (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This describes the distribution of gold nanoparticles at the BBB.

claim: Sections collected on conventionally coated ccKapton or carbon nanotube tape were stuck to the tape despite treatment with organic solvents and any other chemical or physical treatments tested.
source: However, such sections were stuck to the tape despite treatment with organic solvents and any other chemical or physical treatments that we tested (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the initial challenge in developing the ATUM-Tomo method.

claim: An ultrathin tissue section could be removed from Formvar-coated tape by incubation in chloroform or 1,2-dichlorethan.
source: Short ccKapton tape strips were Formvar-coated using a standard film casting device (cfcKapton), onto which 100–300 nm tissue sections were collected from the diamond knife water bath. Indeed, such sections could be recovered from the tape by incubation in chloroform or 1,2-dichlorethan.
evidence: This describes a successful approach to section recovery.

claim: Formvar coating induced charging, depending on the thickness of the coat.
source: We found that Formvar coating induced charging, depending on the thickness of the coat (Figure 2D).
evidence: This describes a problem with Formvar coating for SEM imaging.

claim: Imaging at high resolution (<10 nm) prevented subsequent section detachment.
source: In addition, imaging at high resolution (<10 nm) prevented subsequent section detachment (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the Formvar coating approach.

claim: Sections attached to cpcKapton using permanent marker could be detached by intense rinsing with acetone.
source: We labeled ccKapton with a thin film of permanent marker with a wide tip (cpcKapton) and found that sections attached to such tape could be detached by intense rinsing with acetone.
evidence: This describes the successful development of the permanent marker coating method.

claim: Coatings with permanent marker of red color, but not black color partially detached from the plastic support and lead to strong charging during SEM imaging.
source: Coatings with permanent marker of red color, but not black color partially detached from the plastic support and lead to strong charging during SEM imaging (Figure 2D).
evidence: This describes differences between marker colors in the coating approach.

claim: Tissue sections attached to cpcKapton, using pens of either color, showed major tissue section folds.
source: Tissue sections attached to cpcKapton, using pens of either color, showed major tissue section folds (Figure 2D).
evidence: This describes a problem with the initial marker coating approach.

claim: Plasma-discharged cpcKapton enabled reversible section attachment at certain SEM imaging conditions (10 nm lateral resolution at 3 µs dwell time) with ultrastructural quality comparable to ccKapton.
source: Such plasma-discharged cpcKapton enabled reversible section attachment at certain SEM imaging conditions (10 nm lateral resolution at 3 µs dwell time) with ultrastructural quality comparable to ccKapton (Figure 2G).
evidence: This describes the successful optimization of the marker coating method.

claim: Despite extensive acetone rinsing the sections stayed intact with well-preserved ultrastructure.
source: Despite extensive acetone rinsing the sections stayed intact with well-preserved ultrastructure.
evidence: This describes the quality of sections after the detachment process.

claim: The en bloc embedding provided strong TEM image contrast without further post staining.
source: The en bloc embedding provided strong TEM image contrast without further post staining.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the sample preparation method.

claim: Dark deposits were detected on some regions of the section, which probably originate from tissue contact with the coating and accordingly are only superficial.
source: However, we detected dark deposits (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A) on some regions of the section, which probably originate from tissue contact with the coating and accordingly are only superficial.
evidence: This describes a minor artifact of the method with an interpretation.

claim: Serial 400 nm semi-thick sections of the lesion area covering the entire volume of the vibratome section resulted in 250 sections that can be mounted onto one or two wafers.
source: We collected serial 400 nm semi-thick sections of the lesion area covering the entire volume of the vibratome section on cpcKapton. Typically, this resulted in 250 sections that can be mounted onto one or two wafers, dramatically speeding up the correlation process compared to ATUM-SEM (1000 sections on four wafers).
evidence: This describes the efficiency advantage of ATUM-Tomo for this application.

claim: Colloidal gold fiducials (20 nm diameter) needed for image reconstruction could be attached to the surface of sections despite previous SEM imaging.
source: We found that colloidal gold fiducials (20 nm diameter) needed for image reconstruction could be attached to the surface of these sections despite previous SEM imaging.
evidence: This describes a technical capability of the ATUM-Tomo method.

claim: Tomographic reconstructions of semi-thick sections removed from cpcKapton showed surface contamination only at the side that was facing the permanent marker coat.
source: Tomographic reconstructions of semi-thick sections removed from cpcKapton showed surface contamination only at the side that was facing the permanent marker coat (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This describes the localization of contamination artifacts.

claim: The superficial contamination caused reconstruction artifacts in the back projection down to a depth of up to 50 nm into the section.
source: The superficial contamination caused reconstruction artifacts in the back projection down to down to a depth of up to 50 nm into the section.
evidence: This quantifies the extent of contamination artifacts.

claim: Sections that were collected at a nominal cutting thickness of 400 nm showed an actual thickness of 260–300 nm after the tomographic reconstruction.
source: Sections that were collected at a nominal cutting thickness of 400 nm showed an actual thickness of 260–300 nm after the tomographic reconstruction.
evidence: This describes section collapse during ET.

claim: Variable lateral shrinkage of about 20% and minor distortions were detected between the SEM and TEM images of ultrathin sections, probably due to beam damage and acetone treatment.
source: Moreover, we detected variable lateral shrinkage of about 20% and minor distortions between the SEM and TEM images of ultrathin sections, probably due to beam damage and acetone treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes and interprets distortions in the method.

claim: The sections could be recovered even four months after collection and nine months after SEM imaging.
source: The sections could be recovered even four months after collection and nine months after SEM imaging.
evidence: This describes the long-term stability of sections on cpcKapton.

claim: For all three types of resins (LX112, Epon, and Durcupan), sections could be imaged by SEM, detached and collected onto grids for re-imaging by TEM tomography.
source: Besides Epon/Araldite resin (LX112), we tested the detachment and re-imaging procedure with tissue sections embedded in standard Epon and Durcupan resins (Figure 2—figure supplement 5). For all three types of resins, we were able to image by SEM, detach sections and collect them onto grids for re-imaging by TEM tomography.
evidence: This describes the generalizability of the method across resin types.

claim: The identification of LNDs was facilitated in the ET by the increased resolution compared to SEM images.
source: Moreover, the injected colloidal gold particles and LNDs were accumulated in the vessel lumen, with the identification of LNDs —compared to SEM images—actually facilitated in the ET by the increased resolution (Figure 3E; Figure 3—videos 1–3).
evidence: This describes an advantage of ET over SEM for identifying LNDs.

claim: The endothelial layer showed local edema and detachment from the basement membrane, while tight junctions were still intact.
source: We observed that the endothelial layer showed local edema and detachment from the basement membrane, while tight junctions were still intact (Figure 3E).
evidence: This describes ultrastructural features of the BBB at sites of leakage.

claim: Gold particles were detected in platelet vesicles, vacuoles of endothelial cell swellings, as well as in areas of endothelial detachment from the basement membrane.
source: Gold particles were detected in platelet vesicles, vacuoles of endothelial cell swellings, as well as in areas of endothelial detachment from the basement membrane (Figure 3E).
evidence: This describes the subcellular localization of gold nanoparticles.

claim: Comparing the SEM reconstruction with the one from the corresponding serial ETs clearly showed that SEM imaging visualizes only the section surface resulting in a coarse three-dimensional rendering, while ET provided information of the entire section thickness.
source: Comparing the SEM reconstruction with the one from the corresponding serial ETs (Figure 4A) clearly showed that SEM imaging visualizes only the section surface resulting in a coarse three-dimensional rendering, while ET provided information of the entire section thickness (Figure 4B–D; Figure 4—videos 1–3).
evidence: This compares the information content of SEM versus ET reconstructions.

claim: Earlier studies described endothelial edema preceding FITC-albumin early after middle cerebral artery occlusion.
source: In line with our results, earlier studies already described endothelial edema preceding FITC-albumin early after middle cerebral artery occlusion (Krueger et al., 2015; Krueger et al., 2019), another model system for studying BBB leakiness.
evidence: This contextualizes the current findings with previous literature.

claim: At later stages after middle cerebral artery occlusion, loss of endothelial cell integrity with discontinuous plasma membranes and detachment from the basement membrane was observed.
source: At later stages, these authors observed loss of endothelial cell integrity with discontinuous plasma membranes and detachment from the basement membrane.
evidence: This describes findings from previous studies on BBB leakiness.

claim: The DAB staining of FITC-albumin applied in previous studies masks the endothelial ultrastructure and thus provides compromised EM information.
source: However, the DAB staining of FITC-albumin applied in these studies masks the endothelial ultrastructure and thus provides compromised EM information (Krueger et al., 2019).
evidence: This critiques a limitation of previous methods.

claim: The CLEM approach provides high ultrastructural quality by chemical fixation with glutaraldehyde.
source: In contrast, our CLEM approach provides high ultrastructural quality by chemical fixation with glutaraldehyde.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the current method over previous approaches.

claim: Lectin serves as a marker for intact glycocalyx and its loss indicates early pathological events leading to activation of transcellular transport.
source: Lectin serves as a marker for intact glycocalyx and its loss indicates early pathological events leading to activation of transcellular transport.
evidence: This interprets the significance of lectin staining patterns.

claim: The glycocalyx is critical for BBB integrity by suppressing caveolin1-dependent endothelial transcytosis following ischemic stroke.
source: It was shown that the glycocalyx is critical for BBB integrity by suppressing caveolin1-dependent endothelial transcytosis following ischemic stroke (Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This cites previous work on the role of glycocalyx in BBB integrity.

claim: Intact tight junctions and gold particles in vesicles were detected at sites of BBB leakiness.
source: This is in line with the detection of intact tight junctions and gold particles in vesicles at sites of BBB leakiness in the current and previous studies (Krueger et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes findings consistent with previous literature.

claim: The paracellular pathway seems not to be the first loophole and gains importance starting 48 hr after the injury.
source: In contrast, the paracellular pathway seems not to be the first loophole and gains importance starting 48 hr after the injury (Knowland et al., 2014).
evidence: This interprets the temporal dynamics of BBB leakage pathways with citation support.

claim: ATUM-Tomo is a simple and low-cost method for multimodal EM imaging that combines the strengths of both volume SEM and ET.
source: In summary, we developed a simple and low-cost method for multimodal EM imaging that combines the strengths of both volume SEM and ET.
evidence: This summarizes the key contribution of the study.

claim: ATUM-Tomo enables the consecutive inspection of selected areas of interest by correlative serial SEM and TEM, optionally in combination with CLEM.
source: Our novel ATUM-Tomo approach enables the consecutive inspection of selected areas of interest by correlative serial SEM and TEM, optionally in combination with CLEM.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the ATUM-Tomo method.

claim: ATUM-Tomo can bridge several scales, which is particularly important for ultrastructural analysis of focal pathologies or rare cellular and subcellular events.
source: ATUM-Tomo and also correlative ATUM-Tomo can bridge several scales, which is particularly important for ultrastructural analysis of focal pathologies or rare cellular and subcellular events.
evidence: This describes the scale-bridging capability of the method.

claim: Both imaging modalities (SEM and TEM) are non-destructive, thus allowing re-imaging and hierarchical imaging at the SEM and TEM levels.
source: Both imaging modalities are non-destructive, thus allowing re-imaging and hierarchical imaging at the SEM and TEM levels, which is especially important for precious samples including human biopsies and complex CLEM experiments.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the ATUM-Tomo approach.

claim: ATUM-Tomo opens up new avenues for multimodal volume EM imaging of diverse biological research areas.
source: Thus, ATUM-Tomo opens up new avenues for multimodal volume EM imaging of diverse biological research areas.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the broader impact of the method.

claim: The size of LNDs was 35.66±1.66 nm with a PDI index of 0.113±0.002.
source: The size of LNDs was 35.66±1.66 nm, PDI index 0.113±0.002.
evidence: This provides quantitative characterization of the LNDs used in the study.

claim: Lectin and LND fluorescence was possible with minimal autofluorescence despite perfusion fixation with glutaraldehyde.
source: Confocal imaging revealed that lectin and LND fluorescence was possible with minimal autofluorescence despite perfusion fixation with glutaraldehyde.
evidence: This describes the compatibility of fluorescence imaging with glutaraldehyde fixation.

claim: Plasma discharging increases hydrophilicity and thereby prevents wrinkle formation during serial section collection for ATUM and ATUM-Tomo approaches.
source: Plasma discharging increases hydrophilicity and thereby prevents wrinkle formation during serial section collection for ATUM and ATUM-Tomo approaches.
evidence: This explains the purpose of plasma treatment in the method.

claim: ATUM-Tomo requires several rounds of plasma treatment after marker pen coating as the marker introduces hydrophobicity.
source: In addition, ATUM-Tomo requires several rounds of plasma treatment after marker pen coating as the marker introduces hydrophobicity.
evidence: This describes a specific requirement of the ATUM-Tomo method.

claim: Tilt series were recorded from –60° to +60° with 1° increments at a magnification of 4700 x and a pixel size of 2.572 nm.
source: Using a dual-axis specimen holder (Type 2040, Fishione, USA), tilt series were recorded from –60° to +60° with 1° increments at a magnification of 4700 x and a pixel size of 2.572 nm applying the SerialEM software package (Mastronarde, 2003; Mastronarde, 2005).
evidence: This describes the technical parameters of ET acquisition.

claim: For dual-tilt electron tomography, the grid was rotated for 90° in the XY-plane and the second tilt series was acquired using identical microscope settings.
source: For dual-tilt electron tomography, the grid was rotated for 90° in the XY-plane and the second tilt series was acquired using identical microscope settings (Mastronarde, 1997).
evidence: This describes the dual-tilt ET protocol used.

claim: Endothelial swellings were identified at regions without lectin staining, only showing LND fluorescence.
source: Endothelial swellings were identified at regions without lectin staining, only showing LND fluorescence.
evidence: This describes the correlation between fluorescence patterns and ultrastructural features.

claim: Some microthrombi could serve not only as entry points for nanoparticles, but also for cells from the blood.
source: Thus, we can assume that some microthrombi could serve not only as entry points for nanoparticles, but also for cells from the blood.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observation of neutrophil diapedesis.

claim: Healthy endothelium was characterized by an intact glycocalyx and hence lectin staining in the absence of LND fluorescence.
source: Healthy endothelium was characterized by an intact glycocalyx and hence lectin staining in the absence of LND fluorescence.
evidence: This describes the fluorescence signature of healthy BBB.

claim: The required rinsing time for section detachment increases with previous beam exposure of the section in the SEM.
source: In our experience, the required rinsing time increases with previous beam exposure of the section in the SEM.
evidence: This describes an empirical observation about the detachment process.

claim: Through the detachment from the tape in the acetone bath, sections could be physically flipped on the water bath relative to the sectioning direction.
source: However, through the detachment from the tape in the acetone bath, it could happen that the sections were physically flipped on the water bath relative to the sectioning direction.
evidence: This describes a potential complication of the section transfer process.

claim: Vesicular transport might be involved in BBB leakiness based on the existence of morphologically normal tight junctions visualized by ATUM-SEM.
source: The existence of morphologically normal tight junctions visualized by ATUM-SEM suggests that vesicular transport might be involved.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of intact tight junctions at sites of leakage.

claim: ATUM-Tomo provides an integrated view of the cellular environment as well as the ultrastructural features of the compromised BBB.
source: Here, we demonstrate that triple correlation using confocal microscopy, volume SEM in combination with ET provides an integrated view of the cellular environment as well as the ultrastructural features of the compromised BBB.
evidence: This summarizes the capability demonstrated in the application.

claim: ATUM-Tomo in combination with CLEM is a powerful multimodal approach, enabling a bridging of scales from the mm to the nm range.
source: Our application shows that ATUM-Tomo in combination with CLEM is a powerful multimodal approach, enabling a bridging of scales from the mm to the nm range.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the scale-bridging capability.
